page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated virtual CPUs. To address data sets with large working memories, it integrates 1024 GB of DDR4 system RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an allocation ratio of 16 GB of memory per core. The host includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and supports a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps. It does not include discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent compute and data processing capabilities across multiple categories. In PassMark testing, the instance achieved 56,725.09 for overall CPU score, 52,803.60 in encryption workloads, and 26,134.77 in database operations, each positioning within the top 25 percent of results. Clang-based compilation tests scored 40,360.00, also within the top quartile. Measured memory bandwidth registers at 166.56 GB/s for large uncached read sequences and 68.28 GB/s for write operations. Static web server throughput reaches 46.18 GB/s, while in-memory operations like Redis SET commands record 52.78 million operations per second.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the extreme focus on memory density rather than specialized GPU acceleration or compute-heavy scaling. With a 16:1 ratio of memory to vCPUs, the configuration is cost-effective from a resource-density perspective, allowing large working sets to reside in memory on a single node without requiring horizontal scaling across multiple instances. Because local storage is directly attached NVMe media, it provides high I/O throughput for transient data, though persistence requires external network storage. Appropriate workloads include enterprise in-memory databases, Redis caches, real-time analytics engines, and large-scale data engineering pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x2idn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores at 3.5 GHz. The platform is configured with 1024 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering 16 GB per core. The instance includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps baseline networking, without bundled GPUs. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the server delivers top-quartile results in PassMark database operations, hardware cryptographic execution, and software compilation, alongside 166.56 GB/s large-block read memory bandwidth and 46.18 GB/s web serving capacity. This configuration provides high memory density relative to compute allocation, making it well-matched for large-footprint in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, real-time analytics platforms, and big data processing pipelines.
